---
title: "Directory metadata: `_metadata.yml`"
---

## Overview

A `_metadata.yml` file sets options for every document in its directory
and in the directories below it. It takes the same keys as `_quarto.yml`
and as a document's front matter:

```{.yaml filename="posts/_metadata.yml"}
toc: true
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
```

Every document under `posts/` now gets a table of contents and folded
code, without repeating either in its front matter. `_metadata.yaml`
works too.

Directory metadata applies only inside a project, that is, below a
directory with a `_quarto.yml`. Rendering a lone document ignores any
`_metadata.yml` next to it.

## Which files apply

Quarto reads every `_metadata.yml` from the project root down to the
document's own directory, and merges them with the project and the
document. Later entries in this list override earlier ones:

1. `_quarto.yml` (with any active [profile](profiles.qmd)).
2. `_metadata.yml` in the project root, next to `_quarto.yml`.
3. `_metadata.yml` in each subdirectory on the way to the document,
   outermost first.
4. The document's front matter.

So for `posts/2026/launch.qmd`, the files that apply are `_quarto.yml`,
`_metadata.yml`, `posts/_metadata.yml`, `posts/2026/_metadata.yml`, and
the document, in that order. Any of the `_metadata.yml` files can be
missing.

A root `_metadata.yml` is useful when a tool owns the project's shared
settings (a theme, figure defaults) and you want to keep them apart from
the `_quarto.yml` you edit.

## Paths

A relative path in a `_metadata.yml` (a `theme:` SCSS file, a `css:`
file, an `include-in-header:` file) is relative to the directory of that
`_metadata.yml`, not to the document. See [Paths in websites](paths.qmd).

## Differences from Quarto 1

- A `_metadata.yml` in the project root applies to every document in the
  project. Quarto 1 applies it only to the documents directly in the
  root, and not to those in subdirectories.
